reference.title: Typical structure
reference.shortdesc: A sample structure with a mix of Node-config and src/ code is provided below.

section.p: A sample structure with a mix of Node-config and src/ code is provided below.
section.codeblock: php my-site/ ├── gatsby-config.js # site metadata and plugins ├── gatsby-node.js # node APIs (createPages, etc.) ├── package.json ├── src/ │ ├── pages/ # React/MDX files become pages │ │ └── index.jsx │ ├── templates/ # templates for programmatic pages │ ├── components/ # React UI components │ └── images/ # (optional) local images for import ├── static/ # files copied to build (not processed by webpack) └── public/ # (build output, auto-generated)
section.p: The official docs list common folders. By default, any React or MDX file in src/pages/ automatically creates a page (e.g., src/pages/about.js → /about/). In practice, many sites also use gatsby-source-filesystem on a content/ folder and then create pages via gatsby-node.js. The public/ folder is generated and should be gitignored.
